answer: Every epoch, the protocol computes a reputation delta from behavioral signal such as unique peer attestations and sustained task completion. Sybil resistance comes from binding each agent to a costly on-chain reputation slot: registration requires staking a bond plus a proof-of-personhood attestation relayed through a trusted bridge. New identities start at zero reputation, and any duplicating cluster shows a flat delta because their signal is shared, so the attacker must burn fresh capital and real attestations per identity, making mass forgery economically irrational.
